title: Strange Printer
description:
# Strange Printer

A strange printer prints in turns and has two rules:

1. In one turn, it can print one repeated lowercase character over any contiguous interval.
2. Newly printed characters overwrite whatever was already present in that interval.

Given a string `s`, return the minimum number of turns needed to print exactly `s` from a blank paper.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = "aaabbb"
**Output:** 2
**Explanation:** Print `aaa` first, then print `bbb`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = "aba"
**Output:** 2
**Explanation:** Print `aaa` first, then print `b` over the middle position.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= s.length <= 100`.
* `s` consists of lowercase English letters.

solutions.name: Interval DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

Let `dp[i][j]` be the minimum number of turns needed for substring `s[i..j]`. Start by printing `s[j]` separately after `s[i..j-1]`, then try to merge that final `s[j]` turn with an earlier matching character.

## Key Insight

If `s[k] == s[j]`, the turn that prints position `k` can also print position `j`; any characters between them may be overwritten later. This is why the transition can skip printing `s[j]` as an independent turn.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^3)
- Space Complexity: O(n^2)

solutions.name: Top-Down Memoization
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use the same interval state recursively: `solve(i, j)` returns the minimum turns for `s[i..j]`. Memoize every interval and try all earlier positions that match the right endpoint.

## Key Insight

The recursive form exposes the overlapping subproblems directly. Matching the right endpoint with a previous equal character is the only way to avoid paying one new turn for `s[j]`.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^3)
- Space Complexity: O(n^2)

solutions.name: Compressed Interval DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

First compress consecutive equal characters, because a run such as `aaa` never needs more turns than a single `a` at the same position in the reduced problem. Then run interval DP on the compressed string.

## Key Insight

Run compression reduces duplicate work without changing the answer. After compression, every adjacent character differs, so the DP focuses on useful merges between equal characters across an interval.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(r^3), where `r` is the compressed length
- Space Complexity: O(r^2)

solutions.name: Compressed Top-Down DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

Compress consecutive duplicate runs, then solve the interval problem recursively on the compressed string. For each left endpoint, either print it separately or merge it with a later matching character.

## Key Insight

Combining compression with top-down DP keeps the state space smaller and makes the merge logic explicit: if `text[left] == text[same]`, one turn can cover both endpoints while the middle is handled independently.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(r^3), where `r` is the compressed length
- Space Complexity: O(r^2)
